html:
The Assiniboine, or Nakoda, are an Indigenous people of the northern Plains, now living mainly in Saskatchewan, Alberta, Manitoba, northern Montana and North Dakota.

They speak a Siouan language and separated from the Yanktonai Dakota, probably before 1640. Moving north and west, they became close allies of the Cree, and in the 1700s the two peoples formed the Iron Confederacy.

With the Cree they were middlemen of the fur trade. They carried furs to the Hudson's Bay Company posts on Hudson Bay and sold guns and metal goods to the peoples further west. On the plains they hunted bison on foot and then on horseback, and fought the Blackfoot and the Lakota. Smallpox epidemics in 1780 and 1837 killed a large share of them. Today they live on reserves in Canada and on the Fort Peck and Fort Belknap reservations in Montana.
sum: The Assiniboine, or Nakoda, are an Indigenous people of the northern Plains, now living mainly in Saskatchewan, Alberta, Manitoba, northern Montana and North Dakota.
